# 4. A common velocity reset in the coupled system

Here the Lorentz force must be estimated explicitly.

Use the supplied enlarged-family erasing carrier \(w\), and write
\[
u=w+v.
\]
Within a word macro, let \(Q\) solve the Euler linearized equation and \(\mathcal M\) the induction equation:
\[
Q_t=-L_wQ,\qquad \mathcal M_t=-C_w\mathcal M.
\]
Set
\[
v=Qz,\qquad B=\mathcal M b.
\]

The supplied small-word estimates, together with the explicit induction transport, make both conjugated diffusions coercive in \(H^1\). At a word boundary, the velocity coordinate is multiplied by \(W(s)\), while the magnetic coordinate has no jump. The accumulated velocity-coordinate norm loss is controlled by \(ns^5\).

With
\[
E_v=\|z\|_{H^1}^2,\quad E_b=\|b\|_{H^1}^2,\quad
D_v=\|z\|_{H^2},\quad D_b=\|b\|_{H^2},
\]
the joint estimate is
\[
(E_v+E_b)'
+c(\nu D_v^2+\rho D_b^2)
\le C\mu^{-3}(E_v+E_b)^3+C\mu^{-1}.                              \tag{4.1}
\]
The last term permits disturbances and force errors bounded by a fixed constant.

More importantly, the velocity separately satisfies
\[
E_v'+c\nu D_v^2
\le
C\nu^{-3}E_v^3
+C\nu^{-1}E_b^{3/2}D_b
+C\nu^{-1}.                                                     \tag{4.2}
\]
If the magnetic \(H^1\) budget is \(K_\star\), then
\[
\int_0^\delta D_b^2\,dt\le CK_\star^2/\rho,
\]
so the integrated Lorentz contribution in (4.2) is at most
\[
C\nu^{-1}\rho^{-1/2}K_\star^4\delta^{1/2}.                       \tag{4.3}
\]

\[
0<r_0\le r\le1,\qquad K_\star\ge1,
\]
and the incoming velocity satisfies \(\|u_{\rm in}\|_{H^1}\le r/8\).
